title: Plynth Fab source, version 1
description: Written by core as source.fab.json in an import's work folder (core/include/plynth/core/catalog/FabZip.h) and read by the Blender worker: the cleanup_asset format fab and the cleanup_material source kind fab. It says which entries of a Fab zip to unpack and use. The worker unpacks only the entries in files, refusing absolute paths and .. parts, into unpack_folder, keeping their paths. Entry names are as Python's zipfile gives them, with forward slashes. Other paths are absolute with forward slashes.

zip.description: The Fab zip the user picked.

unpack_folder.description: An empty folder in the import's work folder.

files.description: Every entry to unpack: the model, its .bin and .mtl companions, the textures and the metadata. Sorted, no repeats.

model.description: The model entry to read; null for a material.

model_format.description: The worker importer that reads the model; null for a material.

textures.description: The images to build materials from, matched to channels by their file names with the worker's name table. For a model, a material whose own image textures all load keeps them; the others get the set of textures whose name, without its channel word and the prefixes T_, M_, MI_ and MAT_, matches the material's name, or the only set when there is one. Unused textures give unused_image, a material left without a base color gives missing_texture, several images for one channel give ambiguous_map.

metadata.description: A .json entry the worker may read for the item's name and, for a material, its real world size. null for none. Unknown content is ignored.

maps.description: Textures the user picked by hand, by material name, or * for every material. They win over the name matching. A material zip uses only *.

normal.description: auto reads the convention from the normal map's name (gl or opengl, dx or directx) and takes OpenGL otherwise. DirectX maps get their green channel flipped.

entry.description: A file entry of the zip, also listed in files.
